newsitem.title: USA: Alumax earnings continue to improve.
newsitem.headline: Alumax earnings continue to improve.

text.p: Alumax Inc said Wednesday earnings continue to improve from second-half 1996 levels and orders are ahead of the year ago pace.

The company reported first-quarter 1997 net earnings of $26.7 million, $0.48 per share, off a bit from $28.5 million, or $0.52 per share fully diluted, a year ago before gains of $48.6 million from the sale of a 23 percent interest in the Mt. Holly primary aluminum reduction facility and dividend income of $18.3 million received from mining investments prior to their sale in the second quarter of 1996.

Alumax said earnings from operations in the first quarter of 1997 were $58.2 million on sales of $701.8 million and aluminum shipments of 251,500 metric tonnes. This is down from $75.1 million on sales of $802.6 million and shipments of 274,300 tonnes in the first quarter of 1996.

"Our overall sales revenues and shipments are lower than in the first quarter of 1996 because we sold several of our fabricated products businesses in September 1996," chief executive Allen Born said.
"I would also point out that our growing downstream operations are consuming more of our primary aluminum production and that accounts for the lower external primary aluminum sales and shipments."

He said "Alumax earnings continue to improve from second-half 1996 levels," adding incoming "orders are ahead of year-ago levels, apparent primary aluminum consumption is outpacing supply, and visible inventories are trending downward."

Born said the "stronger operating results reflect better average pricing for our primary, semi-fabricated and fabricated aluminum products. We're also benefitting from ongoing efforts to control operating costs and from technological enhancements at our primary aluminum plants that are contributing to better overall productivity and product quality."
Born concluded: "We're encouraged by the business conditions that we see."

Alumax said its debt-to-capital ratio stood at 29 percent at the end of the first quarter versus 42 percent on March 31, 1996. In addition, the company's book value per share has increased to $30.40 from $27.39 (fully diluted) last year.
